html:
The Ese Ejja are an Indigenous people of the rivers of the south-western Amazon, on the Madre de Dios, Tambopata and Heath rivers in Peru and the Beni in Bolivia. They speak a Tacanan language, related to that of the Tacana.

They lived as fishers, hunters and farmers who moved along the rivers, and were known as skilled canoe people. The rubber boom around 1900 brought violence and disease to the region, and later missions settled many in villages. Today they number a few thousand, and gold mining on the Madre de Dios threatens their rivers. Their upstream neighbours include the uncontacted Toromona.
